title: Cumulative money invariants and partial-success accounting

threat_model.actor: Authenticated customer, merchant operator, or a repeated provider callback
threat_model.asset: Captured funds, ledger balances, store credit, and payout instructions
threat_model.trust_boundary: Per-request amount check to the cumulative ledger state that conserves value
threat_model.failure_mode: A monetary operation bounds one request against a static reference amount instead of the balance remaining after all committed movements
threat_model.impact: Cumulative refunds, credits, or payouts can exceed the captured value, producing loss that reconciliation detects only after settlement

required_evidence: An amount is captured, refunded, credited, or disbursed under application control
At least one monetary operation can run more than once against the same order, invoice, or balance

signals: A refund or credit handler compares the requested amount with an order total rather than a remaining balance
The guard read and the money write are not in one transaction, or the row is not locked between them
A provider callback adjusts a balance without recording whether that event was already applied
Balances are stored as mutable totals updated in place instead of derived from immutable entries
Application totals and provider totals are compared only by a nightly job, if at all
A refund service accepts any amount below the order total with no lookup of prior refunds

boundary.subject: the order, invoice, or account whose captured value bounds the operation
boundary.object: cumulative refunded, credited, or disbursed amount
boundary.invariant: The sum of committed outbound movements against one captured value never exceeds that value, and every movement is recorded exactly once

signals: Record, for every amount bound in the path, whether it compares against a static reference or a recomputed remaining balance
Enumerate every writer to the same balance, including admin tools, backfills, callback handlers, and support scripts
Check whether the balance read and the money write share one transaction with the deciding row locked
Write the conservation invariant as a sum over committed entries, then compare it with the bound the code enforces
Trace the partial-success path: what stays committed when a multi-step disbursement fails after the first movement
Check which state transitions are supposed to be terminal and whether any monetary path can still act after them
Look for balances held as mutable totals with no append-only entry table to derive them from
Check for a unique constraint on the provider event id or the movement idempotency key
Compare the currency and minor-unit representation used by the guard with the one used by the movement
Replay a sequence of individually valid partial operations against an isolated fixture ledger and compare the sum with the captured amount
Redeliver one synthetic provider event unchanged and record whether the balance moves a second time

steps: Confirm explicit authorization and use an isolated fixture ledger with a stub provider that records instructions instead of moving funds
Capture a known synthetic amount and record the derived remaining balance as the baseline before any refund attempt
Issue repeated partial operations that are each individually valid and compare the cumulative total with the captured amount
Redeliver one provider event unchanged and record whether a second movement is committed
Record the reconciliation delta, the enforcing code node, and the transaction boundary without touching production balances or live provider credentials

false_positive_filters: A check constraint, trigger, or ledger service below the reviewed code already enforces the cumulative bound
The provider rejects over-refunds for this capture, and the rejection is evidenced rather than assumed
The amount is server-derived from an immutable record and no caller-controlled value reaches it
The operation is single-shot by construction because the same atomic write moves the order to a terminal state
The reviewed path is an internal reconciliation tool whose out-of-band approval is already part of the trusted flow

required_evidence: The bound the code actually enforces, quoted from the reviewed path, next to the invariant it fails to enforce
The set of writers that can move the same balance, showing the guard is absent from at least one reachable writer
A safe isolated reproduction in which the cumulative total exceeds the captured amount, with the call sequence recorded
Monetary impact stated as maximum excess value per captured amount and per unit of time
refutation_tests: Search for a lower-layer control — check constraint, unique index on the idempotency key, or ledger service — that would reject the excess movement
Determine whether reconciliation reverses the excess automatically, which distinguishes delayed detection from realized loss
Repeat the sequence through every alternate writer, since one guarded path proves nothing about the others
Reconstruct the amount's provenance to confirm the caller can influence it at all

root_causes: The guard is per-request rather than cumulative: it bounds one operation instead of the sum of committed operations
The balance is a mutable stored total, so no derivation exists that can be checked against the underlying entries
The read that establishes the remaining balance and the write that consumes it are in separate transactions
Partial success leaves committed movements with neither a compensating entry nor a terminal failure state
Provider events are applied without a uniqueness key, so retries and redeliveries double-apply
Rounding, currency, or minor-unit conversion differs between the guard and the movement

variant_strategy.result_contract: EXACT | VARIANT | REFUTED | BLOCKED; exact and variant matches remain hypotheses until verified

remediation.canonical_invariant: Derive the remaining allowance from committed entries inside the same locked transaction that appends the new movement, and key every movement so re-application is impossible
patterns: Keep money in an append-only entry table and compute balances as a derivation, never as an in-place mutable total
Bound each operation by remaining value recomputed from committed movements under a row lock or a conditional update
Back every movement with an idempotency key and a unique constraint so retries and redeliveries collapse into one entry
Model multi-step disbursements as explicit state machines with compensating entries, so partial success is a recorded state rather than a silent gap
Represent amounts as integer minor units with one currency per entry and reject mixed-currency arithmetic at the boundary
Reconcile provider totals against derived application totals continuously and alert on any non-zero delta

assertions: The vulnerable refund variant accepts a second partial refund whose cumulative total exceeds the captured order total
The remediated refund variant recomputes the remaining refundable balance inside the transaction and rejects the excess
The vulnerable discount variant applies the same single-use code more than once without recording redemption
The remediated discount variant records the redeemed code and rejects the replay
Both remediated variants still complete the first legitimate operation, so a blanket denial cannot pass as a fix

calibration.notes: This pack has not completed a reproducible benchmark run and makes no precision or recall claim.

limitations: Fixture ledgers prove the contract shape; they do not establish how a specific provider behaves under redelivery or partial capture
Provider-side limits may bound over-refunds independently, so a code-level gap is not by itself established loss
Cumulative reasoning depends on knowing every writer to a balance, and batch jobs or manual tools are routinely missed
Currency, tax, and fee models differ enough that the conservation invariant must be restated per product before it can be tested
